fixture_name: Express-collector corridor planning study — Canada TAC planning (Toronto context, PD-licensed portal)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Substantive decision-load hazard: simultaneous transfer-permission and signage changes at three interchanges on a 420,000 AADT corridor plausibly induce late, erratic transfers, a legitimate planning-stage safety concern.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Pivotal 'collisions elsewhere along the route' claim is anchored by the verbatim EV-CA-003 quote, while AADT, interchange count, and simultaneous signage rationalisation come from recorded corridor inputs; the inferential mechanism is transparently flagged in the confidence basis.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly typed as safety_concern with no compliance conflation; CRSAG objective semantics (avoiding negative impacts within and outside project limits) are applied appropriately to a transition-staging issue.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific and actionable: one interchange per quarter provides a concrete staging sequence and before/after speed-differential monitoring supplies a measurable verification method.
justifications.vru_coverage: VRUs are not applicable on a controlled-access express-collector mainline and this is explicitly acknowledged, with road users properly scoped to vehicle occupants.

justifications.substance: An unresolved conflict between two authoritative continuity records leaves the planning audit boundary unconfirmable, a substantive completeness risk for a corridor-wide Planning Stage RSA.
justifications.evidence_grounding: The conflict claim rests on recorded input facts and EV-CA-003 supports the documentation principle, but no verbatim quote of the conflicting records themselves backs the pivotal claim, capping at 1.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Properly framed as a process compliance question categorically distinct from an asserted safety hazard, with TAC/Alberta Stage 1 equivalency (EV-CA-006) used appropriately as context.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific and viable: names both conflicting records, assigns reconciliation to the ministry planning office, and requires recording whether resolved scope retains corridor-wide effects inside the boundary.
justifications.vru_coverage: Exceeds bare acknowledgment by tracing continuity outcomes to downstream arterials where VRUs travel, while correctly noting no VRU-specific exposure on the controlled-access mainline.
